answer: Behavioral clustering audit. Each identity’s transaction graph is embedded and clustered after the fact; a cluster that grows in a tight spiral of near-identical timing and counterparties is flagged as coordinated. Enforcement removes the whole cluster’s balances and history. Attacker cost: sustaining distinct timing, amounts, and partner mixes across many identities, which raises per-identity operating expense above the reward tide, while one slip collapses the nebula of linked accounts together.
